open_points.subject: data-directory root
open_points.text: “Every file the store opens itself is opened relative to the data directory it holds open from the start” does not say how the data-directory path itself, including its parent components, is opened or whether symbolic links there are refused.
open_points.question: May the configured data-directory path or one of its ancestors be a symbolic link, and what exact checks must acquire the held directory descriptor?
options: Open every component with O_NOFOLLOW and refuse any symbolic link
Allow symbolic links in the path but refuse links only inside the resulting directory
Resolve the path normally and hold whichever directory it names
open_points.default_guess: Open the data-directory path component by component with O_NOFOLLOW and refuse any symbolic link.

open_points.subject: SQLite files during startup
open_points.text: “the start's check covers them” and “the database file and its journal are opened by SQLite, which Python cannot ask to refuse a link” do not define what happens if either path is replaced by a symbolic link after the startup scan but before SQLite opens it.
open_points.question: What guarantees that the SQLite file checked at startup is the file SQLite opens, or is replacement after the scan explicitly accepted?
options: Accept replacement after the scan under the same-user-or-root rationale
Recheck immediately before SQLite opens, while accepting the remaining race
Use a mechanism outside Python's SQLite API that binds SQLite to the checked objects
Refuse to start unless the files are newly created under exclusive control
open_points.default_guess: Scan immediately before opening SQLite and accept the remaining race as part of the stated same-user-or-root trust assumption.

open_points.subject: SQLite journal mode and auxiliary files
open_points.text: “in SQLite's default rollback-journal mode, which the kernel does not change” does not say how that mode is guaranteed for an existing or restored database, or which concrete rollback mode and auxiliary filenames count as its journal.
open_points.question: Must startup verify a particular journal mode and refuse any other mode, or may SQLite use whatever persisted or build-default mode it finds?
options: Require and verify DELETE rollback-journal mode
Accept SQLite's persisted or build-default mode, including WAL if already selected
Force a named rollback-journal mode at startup
open_points.default_guess: Verify DELETE rollback-journal mode at startup and refuse a database in another mode.

open_points.subject: renamed or replaced data directory
open_points.text: Store-owned files are opened “relative to the data directory it holds open from the start,” while SQLite opens the database and journals by its own pathname mechanism; the text says nothing about the configured directory being renamed or replaced after startup.
open_points.question: After the data-directory pathname is renamed or replaced, must every part of the store continue using the originally opened directory, must store calls fail, or may SQLite and the file areas resolve to different directories?
options: Continue using only the originally opened directory for every store component
Detect the change and fail all store calls or stop the kernel
Permit pathname-based SQLite files and descriptor-relative file areas to follow their respective resolutions
open_points.default_guess: Detect loss or replacement of the configured directory identity and stop before another store change.

open_points.subject: supported Linux host
open_points.text: “A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named” leaves unspecified which kernels, architectures and required Linux facilities qualify, even though A17 and A18 require O_PATH and O_NOFOLLOW and A03 requires namespaces, resource limits and bubblewrap.
open_points.question: Does “Linux” promise operation on every Linux host, or only on hosts satisfying an unstated minimum feature and architecture baseline, and how is a host below that baseline refused?
options: Support every Linux kernel and architecture on which the process starts
Name a minimum kernel, architecture and required facilities
Define support by successful startup feature probes
Let individual startup operations fail when a required facility is unavailable
open_points.default_guess: Treat Linux hosts with the pinned runtime, bubblewrap and all required syscalls as supported, and refuse startup when a required facility fails.
